name: Mapo Tofu
description: Silken tofu simmered in a rich, fiery sauce of fermented broad beans, chili oil, and Sichuan peppercorns. Invented in the late Qing Dynasty by Chen Mapo, a restaurateur in Chengdu. The dish balances t

name: Kung Pao Chicken
description: Diced chicken stir-fried with peanuts, dried red chilies, and scallions in a sweet-savory sauce. Named after Ding Baozhen, a Qing Dynasty official whose title was "Gongbao".

name: Sichuan Hotpot
description: A communal dining experience centered around a pot of simmering, chili-laced broth. Diners cook raw ingredients tableside — from thin-sliced beef to tripe, lotus root, and tofu skin.

name: Jiangyou Braised Pork Intestine
description: A legendary Sichuan dish from Jiangyou County, featuring pork intestines braised to tender perfection in a rich, spicy sauce. Chewy, bold, and definitely NOT for everyone. Dare to take the ultimate Si

name: Husband and Wife Lung Slice (Fuqi Feipian)
description: Thin slices of beef, beef tripe, and offal in a numbing chili oil dressing. The name sounds wild — but the flavor is unforgettable. Brave hearts only.

name: Rabbit Head (Tu Tou)
description: Sichuan's most controversial street snack — a whole rabbit head, spiced and braised. Intense flavor, hands-on eating. Not for the faint of heart.

name: Grilled Brain Flower (Kao Nao Hua)
description: Silky, creamy pig brain grilled on a skewer with chili, cumin, and Sichuan pepper. An acquired taste — but fans call it the ultimate late-night indulgence. Dare to try?

name: Dan Dan Noodles
description: Chengdu's iconic street noodles — thin wheat noodles topped with a spicy, numbing sauce of preserved vegetables, chili oil, Sichuan peppercorns, and minced pork. Originally carried by pole-bearing str

name: Sliced Fish in Hot Chili Oil (Shui Zhu Yu)
description: Tender fish fillets poached in mild broth, then smothered in hot chili oil with dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns. The oil is for aroma, not for drinking — scoop it aside and enjoy the fish.

name: Kaishui Baicai (Boiled Cabbage in Supreme Broth)
description: Perhaps the most deceptive dish in all of Sichuan cuisine. What looks like plain cabbage in clear water is actually the pinnacle of Sichuan's clear-soup technique — a masterwork that shatters the ster

name: San Da Pao (Three Cannons — Chengdu's Loudest Snack)
description: A performance disguised as a snack. Three sticky glutinous rice balls are thrown with force against a wooden board fitted with brass plates — producing three explosive "BANG — BANG — BANG" sounds like

name: Leshan Sweet Glazed Duck (Tianpi Ya)
description: A whole duck brined with Sichuan spices, air-dried, brushed with maltose syrup, then deep-fried until the skin transforms into a glossy, caramelized amber. The crackling-sweet exterior gives way to te

name: Bobo Chicken
description: Cold skewers of chicken, tripe, duck tongue, lotus root, and vegetables steeped in a chilled broth of chili oil, Sichuan pepper, sesame, and aromatics. "Bobo" means earthenware pot in Sichuan dialect

name: Leshan Qiaojiao Beef (Crossed-Leg Beef Soup)
description: A soul-warming beef offal soup simmered with over 30 Chinese medicinal herbs. Clear golden broth, tender sliced beef and tripe, with a subtle aromatic complexity from white peony root, amomum villosum

name: Linjiang Shredded Eel
description: Fresh稻田 eels from Leshan's rice paddies, skillfully deboned with an ox-bone knife into perfect shreds, then quick-fried in pork fat with pickled chilies, Sichuan pepper, and local herbs. The eel shred

name: Suji Fried Rice Puff Candy (Mihuatang)
description: A traditional Leshan sweet snack made from premium glutinous rice, puffed in pork fat and bound with maltose syrup into snowy-white blocks studded with peanuts and sesame. Each bite shatters with a cr

name: Chongqing Hotpot
description: The original Chinese hotpot — a blazing cauldron of beef tallow, dried chilies, and Sichuan peppercorns. Born from Chongqing's dockworker culture.

name: Mao Xue Wang
description: Duck blood curd and tripe simmered in a crimson chili broth. Born from Chongqing's dock culture.

name: Chongqing Xiao Mian (Small Noodles)
description: Chongqing's soul breakfast — alkaline wheat noodles in a fiery blend of chili oil, Sichuan pepper, and sesame paste.

name: Hechuan Peach Slice
description: Paper-thin confection of glutinous rice and walnuts — 180-year-old tradition from Hechuan.

name: Rongchang Braised Goose
description: Whole goose braised in century-old master stock with 30+ spices.

name: Chongqing Youcha (Oil Tea)
description: Silky rice porridge topped with crispy fried noodles and chili oil — a disappearing breakfast classic.

name: Baishiyi Pressed Duck
description: Pressed, smoked whole duck with fan shape and intensely savory cured meat. Qing Dynasty heritage.

name: Wanzhou Grilled Fish
description: Charcoal-grilled whole river fish simmered tableside in chili-laced broth. Three Gorges culinary treasure.

name: Tongnan Coiled Eel
description: Whole baby eels dry-fried into spirals until the bones are crispy enough to eat. Ultimate Jianghu challenge.

name: Nanjing Salted Duck (Yanshui Ya)
description: Nanjing's culinary crown — ivory-white duck, tender and delicately salted, served cold. The 'First Flavor of Jinling' with 2,000 years of history behind each slice.

name: Braised Pounded Eel (Dun Sheng Qiao)
description: A lost art of Jinling banquets — eel pounded with a wooden mallet until melt-in-your-mouth tender, then braised for hours with pork belly.

name: Jinling Lion's Head Meatball
description: A half-jin giant meatball of hand-diced pork, enriched with crab roe and slow-braised for 3 hours. So tender it must be eaten with a spoon.

name: Meiling Porridge
description: A velvety soy-milk porridge created for Soong Mei-ling — rice, Chinese yam, lily bulbs, and goji berries for a nourishing, elegant sweetness.

name: Duck Blood Vermicelli Soup
description: Nanjing's ultimate morning ritual — milky duck bone broth with silky duck blood, vermicelli, and offal. The soul of the city in a bowl.

name: Osmanthus Sugar Taro
description: Baby taros slowly simmered in brown sugar and osmanthus syrup until meltingly tender. The taste of a Nanjing autumn in dessert form.
